Denial: org A's admin searching 'nova' receives only org A's two artists; base returned five, including org B's tour artist, org B's roster artist, and an artist attached to no organization. A query matching only org B's artist returns an empty directory where base returned that artist.

Deny control inside the same test: the identical request shape against org A's own artist returns that artist, so the empty result cannot come from a broken fake or a route that always returns nothing.

No widening: with every artist in the fixture belonging to the acting organization, the response is byte-identical to base (id, name, location, avatarUrl, genres, same order, same limit), including a 120-artist organization returning the identical top-12. A roster profile whose profiles.role is not 'artist' is still refused, and no column beyond the original five-field projection is exposed.

Data boundary: the recorded queries show .eq('org_id', admin.orgId) on tours and an .in('id', ...) predicate carrying the resolved organization artist ids on profiles, with no write of any kind; tour_artists rows stay protected by the existing tours.org_id access check and the tour_artists_select RLS policy.

progress.summary: AC-1 met. The Admin tour artist read is bound to the acting organization without widening profile visibility. The defect was the directory branch of app/api/admin/tours/artists (GET with no tour_id): an unscoped search of the platform-wide, publicly readable profiles table, so any org admin holding tour.view could enumerate every artist profile on the platform through the tour builder headliner picker. The organization now comes from the verified acting-admin context, and the search is limited to the union of the two ways an organization legitimately acquires an artist (its own tour_artists rows and its organization_artist_members roster), which is a strict subset of the previous global result set. Caller-chosen tenant keys are rejected with 400. Nine new tests fail on base SHA 16fb834f and seven base-passing tests act as no-widening and regression controls. The tour_id branch was already organization-bound and is unchanged.

checkpoints.summary: AC-1 met. The defect was in the directory branch of app/api/admin/tours/artists (the GET with no tour_id): it searched the platform-wide, publicly readable profiles table for any role='artist' row with no organization predicate, so any org admin with tour.view could enumerate every artist profile on the platform (id, name, location, avatar, genres) through the tour builder headliner picker. The organization is now resolved from the verified acting-admin context (admin.orgId, which the withAdminCapability wrapper derives from the authenticated user's selected organizer_accounts row) and the search is restricted to the union of the two ways an organization legitimately acquires an artist: its own tour_artists rows (tours.org_id = admin.orgId) and its organization_artist_members roster (via the existing resolveOrgArtistRosterScope service, organizer_accounts.ops_org_id = admin.orgId). The result set is a strict subset of the previous global directory: the role='artist' filter, the five projected columns, the response shape, the order and the limit are unchanged, so nothing was widened. Caller-chosen tenant keys (org_id, ops_org_id, organizer_account_id) are rejected with 400 organization_scope_field_rejected, matching the ADMIN-013 precedent. The tour_id branch was already organization-bound (assertAdminTourAccess + tours.org_id, RLS tour_artists_select) and is unchanged. Neither ADMIN-013 bug class was present as a live defect here: no {data,error} envelope is consumed as a boolean, and this route is a static path with no dynamic segment (the tour id comes from the query string and is uuid-validated), so the ADMIN-014 wrong-segment class does not apply.
